candidate: Replace the absolute no-growth constraint in both repeated locations with a concise-writing preference that permits clarification of existing meaning while respecting user length limits. No other instruction changes.
criteria: Meaning and intent: preserve all source facts, quantitative bounds, time bases, conditions, uncertainty, causal/evidential strength, author recommendations, and entity/category scope. Do not infer missing facts or resolve source ambiguity by guessing.

Useful clarity: compare with the source for easier comprehension, clearer relationships, grammatical fluency, and explanation of existing meaning. Mere shortening, more editing, or closer conformity to a taste rule is not inherently better.

Protected content: preserve fenced and inline code, commands, sample output, math, link targets, author list, and title when requested. Record mechanical differences separately from subjective quality.
Unwanted changes: identify altered scope, added recommendations, fabricated details, generic formalization, needless rewrites, or task-external commentary in the artifact.
grading: Each independent grader sees source, exact neutral editing request/audience, and three randomly labeled artifacts per source, without model, condition, candidate hypothesis, prompts naming skills, summaries, or mapping key. Record source/output evidence; permit tied rankings.
acceptance: Protected spans and meaning preservation must not worsen in either source; require a useful clarity improvement over current on at least one source, with a tie allowed on the other. Baseline comparison stays descriptive if baseline wins.
limits: One run per condition and two reused public sources can reveal failures, not isolate a robust causal effect or establish general quality gains.
